name: MealWise
subcategory: AI recipe generation for budget-aware home cooking
tagline: Turn one natural-language meal request into a practical, budget-aware recipe.

pricing.notes: US reference prices; Apple shows the binding local price and billing terms before purchase.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan includes 15 recipe generations per calendar month, text and voice requests, local saving, and no advertising.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 15 recipe generations per calendar month; text and voice requests; local recipe library.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 80 recipe generations per calendar month plus per-serving nutrition estimates when available.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: No monthly product quota, subject to fair use and abuse protection; recipe refinement and regeneration; optional cloud sync when publicly activated.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 15 recipe generations per calendar month at launch.
pricing.billingTerms: Monthly or yearly auto-renewing subscriptions through Apple; cancel in Apple subscription settings.
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI generation remains subject to fair-use and abuse controls; Apple displays taxes and any offer eligibility before purchase.

verdictSummary: A useful personal version is absolutely one-shottable: a small local app can turn a typed meal request, ingredients, budget, servings and time into a structured recipe. What does not arrive in one session is MealWise's native iPhone finish, voice input, authenticated quota enforcement, optional cross-device sync, and the ongoing work of keeping AI output reliable and safe to use.
coreLoopDIY: Turn one natural-language meal request into a structured recipe with ingredients, portions, estimated costs and cooking steps, then save it locally.
whatYouLose: native iPhone interaction and voice dictation
server-side authentication, quota enforcement and abuse protection
ongoing AI-quality, food-safety and operational maintenance
moatNotes: The recipe idea itself is reproducible; the paid product mainly buys a finished mobile workflow and ongoing operation.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay when they want a recipe generator that already lives on their phone, accepts voice input, remembers their work locally, and handles account, quota and billing plumbing without a personal API key or a weekend of setup. That is mostly execution rather than a structural moat, but it is still the part that decides whether a personal tool gets used every week.

alternatives.name: RecipeSage
alternatives.desc: A free recipe keeper with planning, shopping lists and an AI cooking assistant; less focused on one-shot budget recipes.

facts.install: Use the hosted web and mobile apps, or self-host with Docker Compose.
facts.dataFormat: Recipes, meal plans and shopping lists are portable through PDF, JSON-LD or text exports.
facts.gapVsPaid: RecipeSage is a broad recipe organizer with an assistant, not a focused prompt-to-budget-recipe flow with cost estimates.

alternatives.name: Mealie
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted household recipe server with imports and meal planning; you bring both the recipes and the server.

facts.install: Docker Compose or a supported manual deployment.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mealie manages and imports a household recipe collection, but it does not replace MealWise's AI-generated budget and per-person cost estimates.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert needs Docker, persistent storage, updates and backups before it becomes a household recipe server.

notes: MealWise is an iPhone app; public pricing is the current US reference price and Apple controls the final local storefront price.
prompt:
Build a personal MealWise-like recipe generator in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, IndexedDB, and the OpenAI Responses API; do not offer alternative stacks.
Make the first run work with npm install and npm run dev.
Add an .env.example containing only OPENAI_API_KEY.
Create one mobile-first page with a natural-language meal request box.
Let the request include ingredients on hand, budget, servings, dietary preferences, exclusions, time and equipment.
Send it to the model with a strict JSON schema.
Render one complete recipe with title, servings, ingredients, estimated ingredient costs, total cost, cost per person, steps and a practical tip.
Clearly label all costs, allergen handling and nutrition-related content as estimates to verify.
Save accepted recipes locally in IndexedDB.
Include a searchable saved-recipe library and deletion controls.
Provide loading, empty, offline, malformed-model-response and retry states.
Validate input and safely render all model output as text.
Keep the API key server-side and never log meal requests or recipes.
Write focused tests for schema parsing and per-person cost calculation.
Create a README with setup, data location, privacy behavior and limitations.
Do not add accounts, billing, analytics, cloud sync, voice input, push notifications or background jobs.
Do not claim live grocery prices, dietary safety, allergy safety, nutritional accuracy or food-safety guarantees.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
